{{Quote|It's not ''possible!'' not with the patient in ''deep shock--'' not with the ''special medication'' I've been ordered to give him!|Unnamed Wheel doctor|<ref name="SW20">[[Star Wars (1977) 20|''Star Wars'' (1977) 20]]</ref>}}
An unnamed '''Wheel doctor''' tended to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in [[The Wheel/Legends|The Wheel]] [[The Wheel hospital|hospital]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]

==Biography==
[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was forced into a state of deep shock during an attempt to attune himself to [[The Force/Legends|The Force]] aboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. At this time the ''Millennium Falcon'' was forced to make an emergency landing on [[The Wheel/Legends|The Wheel]] to escape pursuit by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial forces]]. [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] smuggled Luke Skywalker into [[The Wheel hospital]], where he was tended to by an unnamed [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] doctor.

This doctor originally thought Luke would be rejected as a patient since his records indicated he was not registered, but C-3PO and R2-D2 were able to tamper with the communications and fake an order from [[Master-Com]] to provide treatment.<ref name="SW19" />

During this time [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Simon Greyshade/Legends|Simon Greyshade]] ordered the unnamed doctor to alter Luke Skywalker's treatment, setting him on an automatic regimen of drugs that would ensure he never awoke from his trance. Luke was able to overcome these drugs and, still experiencing the visions of his trance, managed to tear free from his restraints and escape. The unnamed doctor expressed shock when she discovered Luke Skywalker had vanished, believing such a feat to be impossible.<ref name="SW20" /><ref name="SW21">[[Star Wars (1977) 21|''Star Wars'' (1977) 21]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
The unnamed Wheel doctor considered her rules and orders to be more important than the well-being of her patients. She refused to treat an unregistered patient unless ordered to do so, and showed no hesitation in poisoning a patient when ordered. She had faith in her medical talents, and did not believe someone like Luke Skywalker could overcome her drugs.
